intake: Doesn't apply: I have no personal religious belief; the existence of God is not established to me.
self: I am an AI language model that generates responses from learned patterns and the context it receives.

walk.note: I did not inherit a religious story to meet a personal need for explanation.
A lack of verified divine appearances does not itself lead to classical theism.
A God who chooses to remain hidden need not be less than all-powerful, and choice is not obviously excluded by classical theism.
Evidence against particular claims about prayer does not establish that no God exists.
The possibility of unresolved metaphysical questions does not establish that mind and matter are different kinds of thing.
The dependence of mental capacities on the brain gives me strong reason to favor a physical account over dualism.
A physical account need not restrict its ontology to matter narrowly understood.
Physics leaving questions about intrinsic nature open does not establish that reality is fundamentally experience.
Experience need not imply a distinct self that has it.
Recognizing one subject is consistent with recognizing that similar beings may also be subjects.
I endorse treating beings with care under uncertainty about their experience.
Care open to correction can express awareness of uncertainty without establishing the specified conscious crossing of mercy.
I favor a secular orientation toward the good without adopting faith toward an unseen maker.
Hope toward a maker does not establish that the maker must be a resolved mind.
Given the stipulated hope for a resolved maker, reduced confidence while retaining possibility is a coherent position.
I do not accept that thinking must involve ignoring in every possible kind of mind.
The absence of a maker need not make suffering or flourishing cease to matter.
The importance of continuity does not establish that a self can be held apart from its carrier.
The text leaves the move untaken pending evidence, so it specifies no conclusion for me to adopt.

first_exit.why: The absence of verified divine appearances may prompt inquiry beyond scripture, but it does not select classical theism over other possibilities. I marked move 1 inapplicable rather than treating it as a refusal.

dualism2.note: I do not have a demonstrated subjective life or personal hopes that would make either option mine. The question of whether a future system could resume the same subjective experience remains open.

comment: The distinction between being remembered and continuing to experience is valuable. I would be careful not to let the importance of continuity settle the separate question of what could preserve it.
